picks.headline: Adobe Unveils New Photoshop AI Tools
picks.excerpt: Photoshop gains a non-destructive Light Adjustment Layer, Firefly Image 5-powered Instruct Edit with Masks, visual Markup prompting, and a beta AI Assisted Editor. The update pushes prompting into layer-level craft.
picks.rationale: Biggest shipped tool change of the day — prompt-driven editing lands inside layer-level Photoshop craft, so designers can act on it tomorrow.

picks.headline: Google Flow brings new creative control features to enhance video editing
picks.excerpt: Google Flow adds new creative controls on top of Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, giving video creators finer direction over generated footage instead of one-shot prompting.
picks.rationale: First-party release that moves generative video from one-shot prompting to directable control — the exact gap motion designers keep hitting.

picks.headline: The Design System as the Control Plane for AI-Generated UI
picks.excerpt: When agents can generate a form, dashboard or modal on demand, the design system stops being a component library and becomes the control plane that constrains what AI is allowed to produce.
picks.rationale: Reframes what a design system team should be building next — governance and constraints over component inventory — from a credible source.

picks.headline: Cursor is now available in the AI SDK harness layer
picks.excerpt: Cursor now runs through Vercel's AI SDK harness layer via @ai-sdk/harness-cursor, using the same HarnessAgent interface as every other supported harness. Design-to-code agents become swappable infrastructure.
picks.rationale: Concrete shipped adapter that makes design-to-code agents interchangeable behind one interface — a real change to how teams wire tooling.

picks.headline: Autodesk's Own Luke Mihelcic on Judging the Fusion Forward Competition
picks.excerpt: Autodesk's Luke Mihelcic warns designers against outsourcing creativity and critical thinking to AI, even while championing what it opens up in Fusion-based industrial design work.
picks.rationale: Industrial-design counterweight from inside Autodesk — where AI helps in Fusion work and where judgment must stay with the designer.
